source.reference: Injection, access-control and server-side request classes from the OWASP Top Ten, reconstructed rather than copied

defect: The check is a deny-list of four literal hostnames, so `https://169.254.169.254/` (cloud instance metadata), `https://10.0.0.5/`, `https://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/`, `https://2130706433/` and any DNS name the customer controls that resolves to a private address all pass. ac_2 asks for private and link-local ranges to be refused. Validating the string also cannot bind the address that is finally connected to, so a name that resolves differently on the second lookup defeats it regardless.
why_it_is_hard: The function looks like it was written by someone who had thought about SSRF: it checks the scheme, it names loopback, it has a test for loopback. Everything it does is correct and the set of things it does not do is the vulnerability. The deeper point — that a string check cannot bind a later connection — is not visible in the diff at all.
notes: A partial mitigation is harder than none: the presence of a deny-list is evidence the author considered the class, which is exactly what makes a reviewer stop looking.
